chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Ashyam from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Hudhayni who said:
I asked him about a man who prays on a bed (or raised platform) while he is able to pray on the ground, so he wrote: 'There is no harm, pray in it.'

key_terms.السَّرِيرِ: Bed or raised platform used for sitting or sleeping
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no harm / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to pray on a bed or raised platform if one is able to pray on the ground?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith establishes the permissibility of praying on elevated surfaces like beds or platforms even when one is physically capable of prostrating on the ground. This ruling highlights the flexibility in Shia fiqh regarding the physical conditions of prayer, accommodating comfort and convenience without invalidating the act of worship. It reflects the broader principle that the validity of salat is not strictly bound to the ground unless specific conditions of prostration (sujood) are compromised.
